headline: Quantum Economics, Bound States, and Rare Events
summary: Today's papers explore the practical and theoretical limits of quantum systems, spanning cost-benefit analyses of quantum advantage in chemistry and the fundamental physics of bound magic and steering. Researchers are finding new boundaries for what quantum hardware can achieve and how non-classical resources behave.

themes.title: Quantum Advantage and Chemistry Economics
themes.body: Evaluating the real-world utility of quantum algorithms against classical benchmarks and developing new computational frameworks for excited states.

themes.title: Fundamental Resource Theory and Bound States
themes.body: Uncovering strict limitations in quantum resource distribution, including bound magic states that cannot be distilled and exact monogamy bounds for steering.

themes.title: Open Quantum Dynamics and Rare Events
themes.body: Advancing transition path sampling to model ultra-rare quantum transitions in non-Markovian open environments down to probabilities of 10⁻⁸.

connections.body: Both papers deal with fundamental resource restrictions and convertibility limitations in multi-party or multi-qubit quantum systems.
